name: ima-ai-tools
description: Curated Claude Code skills for the team. Entries reference upstream repositories or plugins kept under plugins/ in this repository.

plugins.name: cc-spend
plugins.description: Reports the API-equivalent cost of your Claude Code usage from local transcripts, for this month or a named one, and gives at most one usage tip.

whenToUse: The month is ending and you want the API-equivalent figure for it.
You suspect long resumed sessions are where the tokens go.
You want to compare your consumption with the subscription price.
metadata.note: Needs Python 3.9+ on PATH. On Windows the interpreter is `python`. The first run fetches the LiteLLM price table and needs network; after that a cached copy keeps working offline. Reads only `~/.claude/projects`; nothing leaves the machine. Then type `/cc-spend`.

plugins.name: grilling
plugins.description: A relentless interview that stress-tests a plan, decision, or idea until the holes show.

whenToUse: A plan looks solid and you want it attacked before you commit to it.
You are about to make a decision you will live with for months.
A spec has gaps you can feel but cannot name yet.
metadata.note: Type `/grill-me` to start the interview on demand.

plugins.name: handoff
plugins.description: Compacts the current conversation into a handoff document another agent can pick up.

whenToUse: The context window is filling up and the work is not done.
You are handing the task to another session or a teammate tomorrow.
A long investigation produced state worth carrying over, not re-deriving.

plugins.name: skill-creator
plugins.description: Creates new skills, improves existing ones, and measures whether they actually trigger.

whenToUse: You are writing your first skill and want the canonical structure.
A skill exists but does not trigger when it should.
You want to eval a skill's performance instead of guessing.

plugins.name: frontend-design
plugins.description: Anthropic's guidance for distinctive, intentional UI — aesthetic direction that does not read as templated defaults.

whenToUse: You are building new UI and want it to not look like a template.
An existing screen works but reads as generic defaults.
A demo or an internal page must look presentable and there is no designer around.

plugins.name: agent-browser
plugins.description: Browser automation CLI for agents: navigate, fill forms, click, screenshot, extract data.

whenToUse: A change needs checking in a real browser, not just in tests.
You want the agent to click through a flow or take screenshots.
Scraping or automating a site would be faster than doing it by hand.
metadata.note: Install the CLI once: `npm i -g agent-browser && agent-browser install`.

plugins.name: sideshow
plugins.description: A live visual surface in your browser: the agent publishes HTML previews, your comments stream back as notifications.

whenToUse: You need to see a diagram or a UI sketch to judge it, not read a description of it.
You want to comment on a specific part and have the agent pick that up mid-task.
metadata.note: Needs Node 22.18+. Run the viewer once with `npx -y sideshow serve --open` and keep it running. The install asks for the viewer URL (local default `http://localhost:8228`). Restart the session — MCP servers start on session start.

plugins.name: context-mode
plugins.description: Keeps big tool output out of the context window: sandboxed execution, persistent session memory, searchable findings.

whenToUse: Long sessions die on log dumps, big diffs, or test output.
You want earlier findings searchable instead of re-derived.
metadata.note: Needs Node. The MCP server starts on the next session.
